thread:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak I'm seeing reproducible Inf/NaN downstream when running paged KV + flash attention in reduced-precision runs.

maria: Repro steps: small local run with paging + KV concat on a long chat (approx 10 pages). A100, driver 525. After ~100–140 generated tokens logits contain inf.

maria: repro snippet:
```
# simplified repro
model = load_model("redwood/opt-6.7b-quant-fp8")
ctx = generate_with_paging(model, history_chunks, use_flash_variant=True, dtype=torch.float16)
# after ~120 tokens -> logits has inf/NaN
```

anish: Which commit and selector flags changed? Trying to reproduce here.

maria: commit 3b9f2a1, selector changes: prefer_flash_for_seq_gt=64, prefer_batched_kv=true.

kelly: I ran the same repro. NaNs show up inside the flash attention softmax when KV pages are concatenated. Looks like the pre-exp max isn't stable across page boundaries — scale drift.

sunil: Quick perf profile on the repro (single-worker):
- bf16/flash: 380 toks/s, no NaNs
- fp16/flash: 420 toks/s, intermittent NaNs
- fp8/flash-quant: 520 toks/s, NaNs are deterministic

sunil: Flamegraph points to a huge spike in exp() operand (>~1e4) immediately before inf/NaN.

maria: Hypothesis: when we merge KV pages we lose a common per-row max normalization, so exp overflows. Lower precision (fp8) amplifies this.

kelly: Quick mitigation: implement stable softmax (subtract row-wise max) in the flash kernel path, or force fp32 accumulation for softmax when seq_len > 128.

anish: fp32 accumulation is safer but costly. Prefer a lighter guard: detect large logits and route to fused-batched kernel (which already uses stable softmax) if any max > threshold.

zoe: We started getting customer error spikes on Dedicated for long-chat workloads overnight. Need a fast mitigation we can roll to prod.

maria: deploy-bot: scheduling rolling canary to rollback kernel-selector flags to commit 3b9f2a0 on prod-dedicated at 03:30 UTC :warning:

deploy-bot: Canary started for eng-runtime/canary-kernelexec @ prod-dedicated-1

kelly: Pushed a local patch that adds a pre-softmax clamp: stable_preclamp in flash_attention.cu. It clamps by subtracting row-wise max before exp and sets a fallback flag if max_logit > 1e3. PR: https://git.reed/rdw/attn/patches/245

anish: Microbenchmarks with the clamp show ~3% perf regression on mid-length sequences, but no NaNs in fuzzed runs. I'll post numbers to perf.

sunil: Added a unit test to test-attn-regression-suite: concat-of-pages scenario across dtypes, assert no inf/NaN post-softmax. CI fuzz added too.

zoe: Ops/AEs — run canary asap and surface to AE leads if rollback required. Customer comms standby.

maria: Short-term action items:
- rollback kernel-selector flag in prod (canary running)
- merge pre-softmax clamp + unit test
- update kernel selection to avoid flash-fp8 for concatenated paging until proven stable
- add telemetry: softmax_clamp_counts and kernel-path telemetry per request

kelly: Long-term: build an FP-aware kernel selector that considers kv_page_count, seq_len distribution, and dtype to pick kernels. Also explore fp8-aware stable accumulation strategies.

anish: I'll add a small fast CI fuzz that perturbs logits (random large values / concatenated page offsets) so we catch this class in pre-merge checks. Run target <5 minutes.

maria: eng-sre-bot: new alert rule created: attn-softmax-nans > 5 in 10m -> page oncall. Also filing a follow-up ticket with repro and perf traces.

eng-sre-bot: Alert rule registered.

zoe: cc @sales-eng for customer-facing note draft once rollback status is confirmed.

maria: If anyone has additional telemetry or edge-case repros (different hw/drivers), drop here. :thumbsup:
